title: Algorithmic Monoculture in Hiring: Replicating the Resume-Screening Correlation on Open Models

original_idea.body:
# Algorithmic Monoculture in Hiring: Replicating the Resume-Screening Correlation on Open Models

**Problem:** Correlated Errors showed monoculture in resume screening - one applicant rejected by all models - using many proprietary models. A clean open-model replication would make the systemic-exclusion risk reproducible.

**Direction:** Replicate on a public/synthetic resume dataset and 6-10 open models. Measure the rate of 'screened out by all' vs independence. Twist: test whether paraphrasing/persona-prompting reduces shared rejection.

**Why it matters:** Monoculture in high-stakes gatekeeping is a concrete near-term systemic harm. A reproducible demo plus a tested mitigation has high counterfactual value.

**Relevant context:** Direct replication of the hiring experiment in Correlated Errors (arXiv:2506.07962) on open models.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Near-term fairness/systemic-exclusion harm, not a path to catastrophic AI risk; broad societal label.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Classification on synthetic resumes plus a paraphrase mitigation; very accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped replication with a clear 'co-rejection rate' metric and mitigation arm.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open models, public data; fuzzy-reward lab-independent evaluation.

novelty.reasoning: Direct replication of a published hiring-monoculture experiment; mitigation twist modest.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Hiring monoculture directly demonstrated in cited work; open-model replication adds little.
